Floods Disrupt Nickel Operations in Sulawesi, Hitting Indonesian Metals & Mining Industry in 2021

Severe flooding in early April 2021 in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, significantly disrupted operations across the region’s metals and mining sector, with Vale Indonesia Tbk PT among the companies affected.

The flooding, triggered by several days of torrential rain, inundated key mining sites and damaged critical transport links essential for the movement of nickel ore and finished metals. According to the Indonesian Mining Association, at least three major mining concessions in the Soroako region temporarily suspended activities as water levels rose, impacting output and delivery schedules.

Vale Indonesia Tbk PT halted production at its processing plant for 48 hours as a precautionary measure after floodwaters encroached on access roads and threatened key infrastructure. In a statement at the time, company spokesperson Andi Saputra said, “Safety remains our top priority. We worked closely with local authorities to monitor conditions and resume operations as soon as it was safe to do so.”

Another mining operator, PT Tambang Hijau Nusantara, reported delays in shipping nickel ore to export terminals due to washed-out rail links and road closures. The company estimated a production shortfall of roughly 6% for the second quarter of 2021 as a result of the disruption.

The Indonesian Nickel Workers Union raised concerns about access to affected sites and the welfare of employees. “Many workers faced difficulties reaching the mines and returning home,” said union representative Diah Pratiwi. “We appreciate the rapid response in ensuring everyone’s safety, but the event highlights the need for better disaster preparedness in mining areas.”

Industry analysts estimate that the flooding resulted in a combined output loss of approximately 8,000 metric tons of nickel in April 2021, with the majority of operations resuming normal activity within a week. According to data from the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, the overall impact on annual production was limited, but the incident underscored the vulnerability of Indonesian mining assets to extreme weather events.

“Infrastructure resilience is now a key focus,” said mining analyst Rizky Hidayat. “Operators are reviewing their flood mitigation protocols and investing in improved drainage and early-warning systems.”

By mid-April 2021, repair works had restored road and rail access, and all affected metals and mining sites had returned to full operations.
